title: Producing Fieldwork Resources for Survey Data Collection
text: Household surveys, agricultural censuses, ground-truth campaigns rely high-resolution satellite imagery delineate Enumeration Areas (EAs), verify building footprints, guide field enumerators sampled structures. vantorr provides dedicated suite fieldwork functions turn Vantor / Maxar satellite basemaps seamline metadata ready--use survey resources: vantor_survey_grid(): Partition Area Interest (AOI) square hexagonal survey index cells labeled "A1", "A2", "B1", etc. vantor_vintage_report(): Audit acquisition dates (acq_time), resolution (gsd), sensor quality Vantor basemap strips across Enumeration Area flag outdated imagery deploying field teams. CSV (.csv) & GeoJSON (.geojson) odk_geopoint ("lat lon 0 0") ODK Collect, KoboToolbox, ArcGIS Survey123. Tab-delimited (.tab) assignment preload tables (output_suso_tab) <gps_var>__Latitude, <gps_var>__Longitude, _target_area World Bank Survey Solutions (direct programmatic assignment creation via SurveySolutionsAPIv2 R package). vantor_field_atlas(): Generate multi-page printable PDF Field Atlas (Map Book) featuring Overview Index sheet zoomed-Enumeration Area detail sheets Vantor satellite imagery, scale bars, north arrows, enumerator sign-footers. vantor_offline_package() & vantor_write_tpk(): Bundle vector layers (.gpkg, zipped .shp), CAPI preload tables (.csv Survey Solutions .tab), georeferenced Web Mercator basemaps (.tif), multi-zoom Esri Tile Packages (.tpk / .tpkx clean _tpk.zip upload archives) portable directory offline tablet apps (World Bank Survey Solutions, QField, Mergin Maps, ArcGIS Field Maps). what: 4. Generating a Multi-Page Printable Field Atlas (PDF Map Book)
title: Producing Fieldwork Resources for Survey Data Collection
text: paper back-maps field supervisor binders, vantor_field_atlas() generates multi-page PDF Map Book containing: Page 1 (Overview Index Sheet): Shows entire AOI, grid cell boundaries labels (A1, A2, …), sample locations. Pages 2..N (Detail Enumeration Sheets): One page per grid cell, zoomed configurable buffer (buffer_m = 50), metric scale bar, north arrow, sample point labels, imagery vintage date, field notes sign-line. authenticated Vantor (vantor_has_auth()), simply set fetch_basemap = TRUE (pass pre-downloaded SpatRaster via raster = ...) render 30 cm 15 cm Vantor Vivid RGB satellite basemap underneath every page PDF atlas:
code: atlas_pdf <- tempfile(pattern = "vantor_atlas_", fileext = ".pdf")  vantor_field_atlas(   grid = vintage_grid,   points = capi_samples,   output_file = atlas_pdf,   title = "Denver Survey Enumeration Atlas",   buffer_m = 50,   fetch_basemap = FALSE, # Set fetch_basemap = TRUE when authenticated to embed Vantor RGB imagery   verbose = FALSE )  file.exists(atlas_pdf) #> [1] TRUE vantor_field_atlas(   grid = vintage_grid,   points = capi_samples,   output_file = "denver_field_atlas.pdf",   fetch_basemap = TRUE,   resolution = 0.3,   product = "VIVID_STANDARD_30" )

title: Interactive Leaflet Maps and Shiny Apps with vantorr
text: Vantor Hub endpoints support two authentication mechanisms distinct scopes: OGC & Non-Administrative APIs (get_maxar_wms_basemap(), get_maxar_wms_tiles(), vantor_get_seamlines()): Work either API Key (maxar-api-key) OAuth2 Bearer Token (Authorization: Bearer ). Account Services / Admin APIs (vantor_get_usage()): Require OAuth2 Bearer Token (vantor_auth(username = "...", password = "...")), Vantor’s Admin APIs accept API keys. Browser-Based leaflet Tile Layers (add_vantor_basemap(), add_vantor_seamlines(mode = "wms"), add_vantor_imagery()): Require API Key (maxar_api_key URL query parameter), web browsers rendering tile requests attach custom HTTP Authorization: Bearer headers. use leaflet tile layers seamlessly, configure API key .Renviron (can also set VANTOR_USERNAME VANTOR_PASSWORD alongside use vantor_get_usage()): register start R session Shiny app:

what: 3. Building a Custom Shiny Application with a Leaflet Map
title: Interactive Leaflet Maps and Shiny Apps with vantorr
text: complete, minimal Shiny application built scratch using leaflet vantorr. allows user : Switch Vivid Standard (30 cm) Vivid Advanced (15 cm) basemaps. Toggle WMS Seamlines cutline overlay. Click Fetch WFS Seamlines load interactive sf seamline polygons current map viewport (input$map_bounds) display metadata table. Click Download Viewport GeoTIFF export visible map extent via get_maxar_wms_basemap().
code: library(shiny) library(leaflet) library(sf) library(vantorr)  # Ensure VANTOR_API_KEY is set in .Renviron or call vantor_auth(api_key = "...")  ui <- fluidPage(   titlePanel("Custom Vantor Leaflet + Shiny App"),   sidebarLayout(     sidebarPanel(       width = 4,       selectInput(         "product",         "Vivid Product:",         choices = c(           "Vivid Standard 30 cm" = "VIVID_STANDARD_30",           "Vivid Advanced 15 cm" = "VIVID_ADVANCED_15"         )       ),       checkboxInput("seamlines", "Show WMS Seamlines", value = FALSE),       actionButton(         "load_wfs",         "Fetch WFS Seamlines in View",         class = "btn-info btn-block"       ),       hr(),       numericInput("res", "Export Resolution (m):", value = 0.5, min = 0.15, max = 5, step = 0.15),       downloadButton("download_tif", "Download Viewport GeoTIFF", class = "btn-success btn-block"),       hr(),       h5("Seamline Vintage Summary"),       tableOutput("seamline_table")     ),     mainPanel(       width = 8,       leafletOutput("map", height = "600px")     )   ) )  server <- function(input, output, session) {   seamlines_rv <- reactiveVal(NULL)    # Helper reactive: convert Leaflet map bounds to an sf::bbox (EPSG:4326)   viewport_bbox <- reactive({     req(input$map_bounds)     b <- input$map_bounds     sf::st_bbox(       c(xmin = b$west, ymin = b$south, xmax = b$east, ymax = b$north),       crs = sf::st_crs(4326)     )   })    # 1. Initialize the Leaflet map   output$map <- renderLeaflet({     leaflet() |>       addTiles(group = "OpenStreetMap") |>       setView(lng = -104.995, lat = 39.740, zoom = 15) |>       add_vantor_basemap(         product = "VIVID_STANDARD_30",         group = "Vantor Vivid",         verbose = FALSE       ) |>       addLayersControl(         baseGroups = c("Vantor Vivid", "OpenStreetMap"),         overlayGroups = c("Vantor Seamlines", "WFS Polygons"),         options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)       )   })    # 2. Update basemap and WMS seamlines via leafletProxy()   observe({     leafletProxy("map", session = session) |>       clearGroup("Vantor Vivid") |>       clearGroup("Vantor Seamlines") |>       add_vantor_basemap(         product = input$product,         group = "Vantor Vivid",         show_seamlines = input$seamlines,         verbose = FALSE       )   })    # 3. Query WFS vector seamlines for the current viewport on button click   observeEvent(input$load_wfs, {     bb <- viewport_bbox()     withProgress(message = "Fetching WFS seamlines...", value = 0.5, {       sl <- vantor_get_seamlines(bbox = bb, product = input$product)       seamlines_rv(sl)     })      if (!is.null(seamlines_rv()) && nrow(seamlines_rv()) > 0) {       leafletProxy("map", session = session) |>         clearGroup("WFS Polygons") |>         addPolygons(           data = seamlines_rv(),           group = "WFS Polygons",           color = "#00E5FF",           weight = 2,           fillOpacity = 0.15         )     }   })    # 4. Render summary table of seamline acquisition dates and sensors   output$seamline_table <- renderTable({     sl <- seamlines_rv()     req(sl)     df <- sf::st_drop_geometry(sl)     cols <- intersect(c("acq_time", "sensor", "gsd", "catid"), names(df))     head(df[, cols, drop = FALSE], 10)   })    # 5. Download GeoTIFF for the current map viewport   output$download_tif <- downloadHandler(     filename = function() {       paste0("vantor_viewport_", Sys.Date(), ".tif")     },     content = function(file) {       withProgress(message = "Downloading GeoTIFF...", value = 0.4, {         get_maxar_wms_basemap(           bbox = viewport_bbox(),           output_file = file,           resolution = input$res,           product = input$product,           return_type = "file"         )       })     }   ) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

Authentication module (auto-refreshes OAuth2 tokens)   auth_state <- vantor_auth_server("vantor_login")    # 2. Explorer module (returns reactive bbox, seamlines, product, and resolution)   explorer <- vantor_explorer_server(     "vantor_map",     auth_reactive = auth_state   )    # 3. Use the reactive bounding box in your own downstream Shiny logic   output$selected_bbox <- renderPrint({     explorer$bbox()   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server) if (interactive()) {   run_vantor_demo_app() }

what: Why Standard macOS .zip Archives Fail on Survey Solutions HQ
title: Creating Spatial Resources for World Bank Survey Solutions Fieldwork
text: users compress .tpk .shp file using macOS Finder (Right-click →\rightarrow Compress), macOS injects hidden AppleDouble resource fork entries (__MACOSX/._filename.tpk). Survey Solutions Headquarters validates every entry uploaded .zip archive via MapFilesValidator.CheckFileNamesOnInvalidChars rejects upload : file __MACOSX/._<filename>.tpk name includes invalid characters. Additionally, files zipped inside subfolder rather root .zip archive, Survey Solutions HQ locate map files extraction. vantorr handles requirements automatically pure R—without requiring ArcGIS Pro, ArcMap, ArcGIS Online credits—using vantor_write_tpk(), vantor_export_capi(), vantor_offline_package(), integrates directly SurveySolutionsAPIv2 package programmatic server uploads assignment creation.

what: 1. Delineating Enumeration Areas, Sample Points & .tab Assignment Preloads
title: Creating Spatial Resources for World Bank Survey Solutions Fieldwork
text: Unlike ODK Collect KoboToolbox (preload CSV/GeoJSON files single space-separated odk_geopoint string), Survey Solutions Headquarters (Survey Setup -> Questionnaires -> Upload Assignments) requires tab-delimited (.tab) preload files specific column naming conventions: <gps_var>__Latitude <gps_var>__Longitude: display sampled households interactive pins Interviewer tablet’s Map Dashboard (overlaid directly top offline .tpk basemap), questionnaire Survey Solutions Designer include Identifying Geography (GPS) question (e.g., variable name hh_gps). Survey Solutions preloads GPS questions via composite column headers separated double underscore (__): hh_gps__Latitude, hh_gps__Longitude, hh_gps__Accuracy, hh_gps__Altitude, hh_gps__Timestamp. _target_area: Survey Solutions’ system column (64 characters) groups assignments geographic sector (cell_id, e.g., "A1", "B2") Interviewer Map Dashboard. plus_code & imagery_acq_date: Preloaded Identifying text questions questionnaire cover page. .tpk satellite basemaps perform turn--turn road routing, enumerators can copy 11-character Open Location Code (plus_code) cover page Google Maps OsmAnd get offline turn--turn driving/walking directions within 3 meters dwelling, switch back Survey Solutions Map Dashboard .tpk basemap final approach. Meanwhile, imagery_acq_date tells enumerator Vantor satellite image captured can distinguish newly constructed buildings older structures. Setting output_suso_tab suso_gps_var = "hh_gps" vantor_export_capi() generates exact .tab file automatically:
code: library(vantorr) library(sf) #> Linking to GEOS 3.12.1, GDAL 3.8.4, PROJ 9.4.0; sf_use_s2() is TRUE  # Define a small Enumeration Area bounding box in WGS84 (EPSG:4326) ea_aoi <- st_bbox(   c(xmin = -105.004, ymin = 39.736, xmax = -105.000, ymax = 39.740),   crs = st_crs(4326) )  # 1. Generate 250m Enumeration Area sub-cells (A1, A2, B1, B2) ea_grid <- vantor_survey_grid(   aoi = ea_aoi,   cell_size = 250,   shape = "square",   verbose = FALSE )  # 2. Define sampled household locations inside the EA hh_samples <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(     hh_id = c("EA01-HH01", "EA01-HH02", "EA01-HH03"),     lon = c(-105.0030, -105.0015, -105.0010),     lat = c(39.7388, 39.7382, 39.7370)   ),   coords = c("lon", "lat"),   crs = 4326 )  suso_tab_file <- tempfile(pattern = "suso_assignments_", fileext = ".tab")  capi_pts <- vantor_export_capi(   samples         = hh_samples,   id_col          = "hh_id",   grid            = ea_grid,   output_suso_tab = suso_tab_file,   suso_gps_var    = "hh_gps",   verbose         = FALSE )  # Inspect the returned sf object (coordinate columns use <suso_gps_var>__Latitude / __Longitude) st_drop_geometry(capi_pts)[, c(   "sample_id", "cell_id", "plus_code",   "hh_gps__Latitude", "hh_gps__Longitude" )] #>   sample_id cell_id   plus_code hh_gps__Latitude hh_gps__Longitude #> 1 EA01-HH01      B1 85FPPXQW+GR          39.7388         -105.0030 #> 2 EA01-HH02      B2 85FPPXQX+7C          39.7382         -105.0015 #> 3 EA01-HH03      C2 85FPPXPX+RJ          39.7370         -105.0010  # Inspect the generated Survey Solutions .tab preload table read.delim(suso_tab_file, check.names = FALSE)[, c(   "sample_id", "cell_id", "plus_code",   "hh_gps__Latitude", "hh_gps__Longitude",   "_target_area" )] #>   sample_id cell_id   plus_code hh_gps__Latitude hh_gps__Longitude _target_area #> 1 EA01-HH01      B1 85FPPXQW+GR          39.7388         -105.0030           B1 #> 2 EA01-HH02      B2 85FPPXQX+7C          39.7382         -105.0015           B2 #> 3 EA01-HH03      C2 85FPPXPX+RJ          39.7370         -105.0010           C2

Zoom 16 (≈2.39 m/px\approx 2.39\text{ m/px}, Scale ≈1:9,028\approx 1:9,028): Enumeration Area road network view. code: if (requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)) {   # Create a synthetic 3-band RGB raster over our EA (in WGS84)   r_ea <- terra::rast(     xmin = -105.004, xmax = -105.000,     ymin = 39.736, ymax = 39.740,     nrows = 128, ncols = 128, nlyrs = 3,     crs = "EPSG:4326"   )   set.seed(42)   terra::values(r_ea) <- sample(60:220, terra::ncell(r_ea) * 3, replace = TRUE)    out_tpk <- file.path(tempdir(), "ea_01_basemap.tpk")    tpk_res <- vantor_write_tpk(     raster       = r_ea,     output_file  = out_tpk,     zoom         = 15:16,     format       = "tpk",     zip_for_suso = TRUE,     verbose      = FALSE   )    # The clean Survey Solutions upload archive is named *_tpk.zip:   suso_zip <- attr(tpk_res, "suso_zip_path")   basename(c(tpk_res, suso_zip))    # Verify the outer _tpk.zip contains only the .tpk at the root (no __MACOSX metadata)   utils::unzip(suso_zip, list = TRUE)$Name    # Verify the internal Esri Compact Cache V1 structure inside the .tpk   utils::unzip(tpk_res, list = TRUE)$Name } #> [1] "esriinfo/item.pkinfo"                         #> [2] "esriinfo/iteminfo.xml"                        #> [3] "servicedescriptions/mapserver/mapserver.json" #> [4] "v101/Layers/_alllayers/L15/R0000C0000.bundle" #> [5] "v101/Layers/_alllayers/L15/R0000C0000.bundlx" #> [6] "v101/Layers/_alllayers/L16/R0000C0000.bundle" #> [7] "v101/Layers/_alllayers/L16/R0000C0000.bundlx" #> [8] "v101/Layers/conf.cdi"                         #> [9] "v101/Layers/conf.xml"

what: Understanding WKID: 102100, MinScale, and MaxScale in Survey Solutions HQ
title: Creating Spatial Resources for World Bank Survey Solutions Fieldwork
text: upload ea_01_basemap_tpk.zip Survey Solutions Headquarters (Survey Setup -> Maps -> Upload Map) click uploaded map view Details / Preview, see metadata extracted servicedescriptions/mapserver/mapserver.json: WKID: 102100: Esri’s canonical authority code WGS_1984_Web_Mercator_Auxiliary_Sphere (EPSG:3857). mapserver.json, Esri stores "spatialReference": { "wkid": 102100, "latestWkid": 3857 }. Survey Solutions Headquarters reads fullExtent.spatialReference.wkid (102100) uses {"wkid": 102100} ArcGIS JS MapPreview widget. Spatially, 102100 3857 identical. MinScale MaxScale: zoom = 15:17, Survey Solutions reports MinScale = 18055.99 (zoom 15 overview scale) MaxScale = 4513.99 (zoom 17 close-scale). interviewer tablet, Survey Solutions configures ArcGISTiledLayer enumerators can pan zoom smoothly across cached pyramid.

title: Creating Spatial Resources for World Bank Survey Solutions Fieldwork
text: addition .tpk raster basemap, field supervisors often overlay Enumeration Area polygon boundaries household sample points Esri Shapefiles Survey Solutions. Survey Solutions imports Shapefile (.shp, .shx, .dbf, .prj), checks .dbf attribute table column named label (case-insensitive). present, Survey Solutions renders labels directly top map Headquarters Map Preview Interviewer app ($feature.label). vantor_offline_package() automates entire bundle single call: Populates label attribute column grid (cell_id, e.g., "A1", "A2") samples (sample_id, e.g., "EA01-HH01"). Exports EPSG:4326 Shapefiles packages <package_name>_shapes.zip root level (subfolders, __MACOSX forks). Generates <package_name>_suso_preload.tab (<suso_gps_var>__Latitude, <suso_gps_var>__Longitude, _target_area) alongside <package_name>_samples.csv. Reprojects raster basemap Web Mercator (EPSG:3857) .tif. Generates <package_name>.tpk <package_name>_tpk.zip.
code: if (requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)) {   suso_bundle <- vantor_offline_package(     grid              = ea_grid,     samples           = capi_pts,     raster            = r_ea,     create_tpk        = "tpk",     tpk_zoom          = 15:16,     create_shapefiles = TRUE,     suso_gps_var      = "hh_gps",     package_name      = "suso_ea01",     verbose           = FALSE   )    # Files ready for Survey Solutions Headquarters upload:   basename(c(     suso_bundle$tpk_zip_path,     suso_bundle$shapefile_zip_path,     suso_bundle$suso_tab_path,     suso_bundle$raster_path,     suso_bundle$csv_path   ))    # Inspect the root-level files inside suso_ea01_shapes.zip:   utils::unzip(suso_bundle$shapefile_zip_path, list = TRUE)$Name } #> [1] "suso_ea01_grid.dbf"    "suso_ea01_grid.prj"    "suso_ea01_grid.shp"    #> [4] "suso_ea01_grid.shx"    "suso_ea01_samples.dbf" "suso_ea01_samples.prj" #> [7] "suso_ea01_samples.shp" "suso_ea01_samples.shx"

Create preloaded assignments via REST API v1 (suso_createASS) # (Assuming this questionnaire has the required ID fields and is loaded) preload_dt <- data.frame(   sample_id         = capi_pts$sample_id,   cell_id           = capi_pts$cell_id,   plus_code         = capi_pts$plus_code,   ResponsibleName   = rep("interviewer01", nrow(capi_pts)),   Quantity          = rep(1L, nrow(capi_pts)) )  suso_createASS(   df        = preload_dt,   workspace = ws,   questID   = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",   version   = 1L )

Interactive leaflet & shiny Integration: Stream WMTS/WMS basemaps, seamlines, archive strips leaflet (add_vantor_basemap(), add_vantor_seamlines(), add_vantor_imagery()), embed drop-Shiny modules (vantor_auth_ui(), vantor_explorer_ui(), run_vantor_demo_app()).

title: vantorr: Access Vantor and Maxar Satellite Imagery APIs in R
text: Vantor API supports API Keys (long-lived, 180 days) OAuth 2.0 Bearer Tokens (session-based, automatic refresh). Note different Vantor API services accept different credential types: OGC & Non-Administrative APIs (get_maxar_wms_basemap(), get_maxar_wms_tiles(), vantor_get_seamlines()): Accept either API Key OAuth2 Bearer Token. Browser-Based leaflet Tile Layers (add_vantor_basemap(), add_vantor_seamlines(), add_vantor_imagery()): Require API Key (maxar_api_key). Account Services / Admin APIs (vantor_get_usage()): Require OAuth2 Bearer Token (username password), Vantor’s Admin APIs accept API keys. can configure credentials .Renviron file (VANTOR_API_KEY, VANTOR_USERNAME VANTOR_PASSWORD) set interactively R session vantor_auth():
code: library(vantorr)  # Option 1: Set an API Key for the session (for OGC & Leaflet functions) vantor_auth(api_key = "your_api_key")  # Option 2: Authenticate via OAuth2 (automatically caches and refreshes tokens; # required for Admin endpoints such as vantor_get_usage()) vantor_auth(username = "your_email@example.com", password = "your_password")  # Check account credit usage and quota (requires OAuth2 Bearer token & Admin permissions) usage <- vantor_get_usage(category = "PRODUCT", unit = "CREDIT")

code: library(vantorr) library(sf) library(terra)  # Define an Area of Interest (AOI) in WGS84 (EPSG:4326) aoi <- st_bbox(   c(xmin = -77.040, ymin = 38.888, xmax = -77.030, ymax = 38.892),   crs = st_crs(4326) )  # Retrieve a 30cm Vivid Basemap directly as a terra SpatRaster basemap_rast <- get_maxar_wms_basemap(   bbox = aoi,   resolution = 0.3,   product = "VIVID_STANDARD_30",   return_type = "SpatRaster" )  terra::plotRGB(basemap_rast, r = 1, g = 2, b = 3, stretch = "lin")  # Fetch vector seamline polygons and acquisition timestamps (OGC WFS) seamlines_sf <- vantor_get_seamlines(bbox = aoi, product = "VIVID_STANDARD_30") large_mosaic <- get_maxar_wms_tiles(   bbox = aoi,   tile_size = 2500,   resolution = 0.3,   merge_tiles = TRUE,   return_type = "SpatRaster" )
